html:
The Yankton, or Ihanktonwan, are one of the divisions of the Sioux, the Dakota speaking peoples of the northern Plains. Their old homeland lay in what is now southwestern Minnesota, eastern South Dakota and northwest Iowa, along the Missouri, James and Big Sioux rivers.

Yankton bands lived by hunting bison, gathering and trading, and from the 1700s rode horses. They held the red pipestone quarry in southwestern Minnesota, source of the stone for sacred pipes, which drew visitors from many nations. The Lewis and Clark expedition met them in 1804.

In 1858 the Yankton signed a treaty giving up most of their land and keeping the Yankton Reservation in South Dakota, where the Yankton Sioux Tribe lives today. Their relatives include the Santee to the east and the Lakota to the west. The Ponca, Omaha and Iowa were nearby.
